claim_text: Renewable energy accounted for 40% of global electricity generation in 2023.

evidence_spans.span_text: Renewables contributed approximately 30% of global electricity generation in 2023, up from 28% in 2022.

claim_text: Global CO2 emissions declined by 10% in 2020 due to COVID-19.

evidence_spans.span_text: Global energy-related CO2 emissions fell by approximately 5.8% in 2020, the largest annual drop on record.

claim_text: China surpassed the US as the world's largest economy in 2015 based on nominal GDP.

evidence_spans.span_text: In 2015, the US remained the world's largest economy by nominal GDP; China surpassed the US only on purchasing-power-parity terms.

claim_text: The IPCC AR6 concluded global warming is likely to exceed 3°C by 2100 under the most ambitious mitigation scenario.

evidence_spans.span_text: Under the most ambitious mitigation scenario (SSP1-1.9), the IPCC AR6 projects global warming of 1.0°C–1.8°C by 2100.

claim_text: Wind energy is currently the cheapest source of new electricity generation globally.

evidence_spans.span_text: As of 2021, utility-scale solar PV holds the lowest levelised cost of electricity for new capacity globally, below onshore wind.

claim_text: Electric vehicles account for over 20% of all cars on the road globally as of 2022.

evidence_spans.span_text: EVs represented approximately 1% of the total global car stock in 2022, though they accounted for a higher share of new sales in some markets.

claim_text: NASA confirmed that 2022 was the hottest year on record globally.

evidence_spans.span_text: NASA and NOAA data ranked 2022 as the fifth-warmest year on record globally.

claim_text: The Montreal Protocol was signed in 1997.

evidence_spans.span_text: The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer was adopted and opened for signature in September 1987.

claim_text: Brazil has the world's largest hydropower capacity.

evidence_spans.span_text: China has the world's largest installed hydropower capacity, far exceeding Brazil which ranks second.

claim_text: The global average surface temperature in 2020 was 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

evidence_spans.span_text: The global average surface temperature in 2020 was approximately 1.25°C above the 1850–1900 pre-industrial baseline.

claim_text: European Union achieved carbon neutrality by 2030.

evidence_spans.span_text: The EU's target is to achieve climate neutrality by 2050; no carbon neutrality was achieved by 2030.

claim_text: Global fish catches have been increasing steadily since 1990.

evidence_spans.span_text: Global marine fish catch has been roughly stable or declining since the late 1980s, with capture fisheries peaking around 86–90 Mt in the early 1990s.

notes: Increasing claim contradicted by flat/declining trend

claim_text: Offshore wind is cheaper than onshore wind globally as of 2022.

evidence_spans.span_text: Onshore wind remains cheaper than offshore wind on a global average levelised cost basis as of 2022.

claim_text: India is the world's second-largest CO2 emitter.

evidence_spans.span_text: The US is the second-largest CO2 emitter behind China; India is typically ranked third.

claim_text: Permafrost covers more than 50% of the Earth's land surface.

evidence_spans.span_text: Permafrost underlies approximately 25% of the Northern Hemisphere's land area, not more than half of Earth's total land surface.

claim_text: The world population reached 8 billion in 2018.

evidence_spans.span_text: The global population reached 8 billion in November 2022.

claim_text: Coal provided less than 20% of global electricity in 2022.

evidence_spans.span_text: Coal accounted for approximately 36% of global electricity generation in 2022.

claim_text: Antarctic ice sheets gained mass on net between 1992 and 2017.

evidence_spans.span_text: A comprehensive study found that Antarctica lost 2,720 Gt of ice between 1992 and 2017, contributing to sea level rise.

claim_text: Global deforestation rates have declined every year since 2010.

evidence_spans.span_text: While overall deforestation rates showed a declining trend, individual years after 2010 (e.g., 2020–2021 in the Brazilian Amazon) saw sharp increases.

notes: Every-year decline contradicted by observed increases

claim_text: The US Inflation Reduction Act committed $370 billion to defence spending.

evidence_spans.span_text: The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 committed approximately $369 billion to climate and clean energy investments, not defence.

claim_text: Solar power is more expensive than natural gas for new capacity in the US as of 2021.

evidence_spans.span_text: By 2021, utility-scale solar PV in the US was cheaper than new natural gas on a levelised cost basis.

claim_text: The Sahel region became wetter from 1970 to 2000 due to increased precipitation.

evidence_spans.span_text: The Sahel experienced severe drought from the late 1960s through the 1980s, with partial recovery in some areas from the 1990s; the period 1970–1980 was characterized by significantly reduced rainfall.

notes: Wetter claim contradicted by drought period

claim_text: The 2021 Glasgow COP26 committed all signatories to net-zero emissions by 2030.

evidence_spans.span_text: COP26 resulted in pledges toward net-zero by 2050 for most countries, with 2030 targets for interim cuts — not a universal 2030 net-zero commitment.

claim_text: More than half of the world's coral reefs have died since 1950.

evidence_spans.span_text: Estimates suggest approximately 50% of the world's coral reefs have been lost since the 1950s, though methodologies vary; the claim of 'more than half dead' overstates the scientific consensus slightly.

notes: More than half vs roughly half

claim_text: Nuclear power is the largest source of low-carbon electricity globally.

evidence_spans.span_text: Hydropower is the largest source of low-carbon electricity globally, ahead of nuclear power.

claim_text: The US exceeded its Nationally Determined Contribution target under the Paris Agreement by 2020.

evidence_spans.span_text: The US withdrew from the Paris Agreement under the Trump administration and did not meet the NDC emissions target by 2020.

claim_text: Biodiversity loss is primarily driven by climate change.

evidence_spans.span_text: According to IPBES, land-use change is the primary driver of biodiversity loss globally, with climate change as a growing but currently secondary driver.

notes: Climate as primary vs land-use as primary driver

claim_text: Arctic summer sea ice could disappear by 2030 under all emission scenarios.

evidence_spans.span_text: Ice-free Arctic summers are projected to become more likely by the 2040s–2050s under higher emission scenarios, and possibly later under lower scenarios.

claim_text: Coal consumption in Asia declined between 2015 and 2021.

evidence_spans.span_text: Coal consumption in Asia continued to grow between 2015 and 2021, driven primarily by demand in China, India, and Southeast Asia.

claim_text: Global water stress affects fewer than 25% of the world's population.

evidence_spans.span_text: Approximately 40% of the world's population is affected by water scarcity according to UN Water assessments.

claim_text: Solar panels have a carbon payback period of over 10 years.

evidence_spans.span_text: Modern solar PV panels typically recoup the carbon cost of their manufacture within 1–4 years depending on location.

claim_text: Fossil fuel subsidies globally were less than $100 billion in 2021.

evidence_spans.span_text: IMF estimates global fossil fuel subsidies (explicit and implicit) exceeded $5.9 trillion in 2020.

claim_text: The EU banned internal combustion engine cars from 2025.

evidence_spans.span_text: The EU agreed to phase out new internal combustion engine car sales by 2035, not 2025.

claim_text: Wetlands store more carbon per unit area than tropical forests.

evidence_spans.span_text: Peatlands and wetlands store more carbon per unit area than tropical forests, making this claim broadly correct — but the evidence refers to peatlands specifically, not all wetlands uniformly.

notes: Broad claim partially correct but overgeneralised

claim_text: The proportion of people living in extreme poverty increased between 2000 and 2019.

evidence_spans.span_text: The share of the global population living in extreme poverty fell from approximately 28% in 2000 to under 9% in 2019.

claim_text: Ocean pH has increased by 0.1 units since the Industrial Revolution due to CO2 absorption.

evidence_spans.span_text: Ocean pH has decreased by approximately 0.1 units since the Industrial Revolution — ocean acidification, not alkalization.

claim_text: Australia relies on renewables for over 60% of its electricity as of 2021.

evidence_spans.span_text: Australia's renewable energy share was approximately 29–30% of total electricity generation in 2020–2021.

claim_text: Global plastic production peaked in 2010 and has declined since.

evidence_spans.span_text: Global plastic production reached approximately 460 million tonnes in 2019, continuing to grow past 2010.

claim_text: All 197 UNFCCC parties submitted updated NDCs before the Glasgow COP26 in 2021.

evidence_spans.span_text: As of COP26, only about 151 of the 197 UNFCCC parties had submitted new or updated NDCs.

claim_text: Food systems contribute less than 10% of global greenhouse gas emissions.

evidence_spans.span_text: Food systems are responsible for approximately 21–37% of global GHG emissions according to the IPCC.

claim_text: Green hydrogen is currently competitive with natural gas for industrial use.

evidence_spans.span_text: Green hydrogen production costs were still 3–5 times higher than natural gas in most markets as of 2021.

claim_text: The Gulf Stream has already completely stopped due to climate change.

evidence_spans.span_text: While AMOC has weakened, scientists have not observed a complete stoppage; modelling suggests possible threshold crossing later this century.

claim_text: Soil carbon stocks globally are smaller than atmospheric carbon stocks.

evidence_spans.span_text: Global soil carbon stocks (approximately 1,500–2,400 Gt C) exceed the atmospheric CO2 carbon pool of around 870 Gt C.

notes: Soil smaller vs larger than atmosphere

claim_text: The US and China signed a bilateral agreement to phase out coal by 2025.

evidence_spans.span_text: No bilateral US–China coal phase-out agreement with a 2025 timeline was concluded; COP26 produced a broader multilateral coal phase-down pledge without a US–China 2025 deadline.

claim_text: Burning biomass for energy is classified as carbon-neutral in all national accounting frameworks.

evidence_spans.span_text: Biomass carbon accounting remains contested; some frameworks allow carbon-neutral classification but the IPCC and many scientists dispute its universal applicability.

notes: All-frameworks claim contradicted by ongoing dispute

claim_text: Sub-Saharan Africa is responsible for 25% of global greenhouse gas emissions.

evidence_spans.span_text: Sub-Saharan Africa accounts for approximately 3–5% of global greenhouse gas emissions.

claim_text: Mangroves have declined in area by 50% globally since 1990.

evidence_spans.span_text: Global mangrove area has declined by approximately 20–35% since the 1980s, with losses slowing in recent decades.

claim_text: The US is the world's largest producer of wind energy.

evidence_spans.span_text: China is the world's largest producer of wind energy by total installed capacity and annual generation.

notes: US vs China as largest wind producer

claim_text: Electric vehicles have no lifecycle carbon emissions.

evidence_spans.span_text: EVs have lower lifecycle emissions than ICE vehicles in most contexts but still produce emissions during manufacturing and through grid electricity depending on the energy mix.

claim_text: Carbon capture removes more CO2 from the atmosphere than global fossil fuel emissions produce annually.

evidence_spans.span_text: Operational CCS captured roughly 40 Mt CO2 in 2021, compared to approximately 33 billion tonnes of fossil fuel CO2 emissions that year.

notes: 40 Mt vs 33 Gt — orders of magnitude apart

claim_text: Africa has the highest per-capita CO2 emissions of any continent.

evidence_spans.span_text: North America and Australia/Oceania have among the highest per-capita CO2 emissions; Africa has among the lowest per-capita emissions.

claim_text: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change was established in 2000.

evidence_spans.span_text: The IPCC was established in 1988 by the WMO and UNEP.

claim_text: Global methane concentrations have been stable since 2000.

evidence_spans.span_text: After a brief plateau in the early 2000s, atmospheric methane concentrations resumed rising from around 2007 and accelerated sharply after 2014.

notes: Stable claim contradicted by resumed rise

claim_text: Japan has committed to closing all nuclear power plants by 2030.

evidence_spans.span_text: After Fukushima, Japan suspended nuclear plants but has since restarted some and as of 2023 was pursuing a policy of restarting and extending reactor lifetimes, not closing all by 2030.

notes: Committed to closure vs restart policy

claim_text: Land-based wind farms are universally opposed by local communities.

evidence_spans.span_text: Studies show mixed community attitudes to wind farms; many projects receive local support, particularly where communities share economic benefits.
